acceptance_criteria: The trace is quoted: finish_reason, completion tokens, and whether content was empty — for the validate call on the -071 run.
A truncated-or-empty reply is a distinct, counted, attributed failure class — demonstrated.
A run ended by that class reaches a typed workflow terminal naming the provider failure — demonstrated by a test.
The runner stop_reason and the workflow terminal remain separate fields — asserted, not merged.
No token budget, model setting, workflow or retry was added or changed — asserted.
The outcome is recorded in HANDOVER.md §6 as a measured fact.
Suite count reported before and after.
assumptions: PR #85's trace is committed under docs/traces/ with the run's name. If it is not, say so and treat the finish_reason as unobserved rather than inferred from the PR body.
The -071 result is a measurement, not a defect in -066 or -067; both instruments behaved correctly or were not reached.
constraints: FIRST, READ THE TRACE AND QUOTE IT, do not work from the PR body: report the validate call's finish_reason, its completion-token count, and whether content was empty or truncated. If finish_reason is not length, the 'truncated reply' framing is wrong — say what it actually was.

THE TWO DEFECTS, and they are separate: (1) a truncated or empty reply from a provider is a distinct failure class — a reply that consumed its whole budget and emitted nothing must not read the same as a well-formed reply that failed validation; (2) a run that ends because of it must produce a typed WORKFLOW terminal naming the provider failure, not stop with only a runner stop_reason.

DO NOT CHANGE validate's token budget, any max_tokens, MODEL_*, or any workflow. The model choice is the owner's (G-2/G-3); raising the ceiling to fit the serving is a config decision and is NOT this command.

DO NOT add a retry for the truncated class unless a retry already exists for schema rejections and this is the same path — if a retry exists, say so and make the truncation class visible to it; if none exists, do NOT add one (that is a behaviour change and needs a ruling).

Record the provider failure as a first-class field in the unit record beside rejections_by_tier, with the serving named (providers_by_function already carries it). A truncated reply must be countable and attributable to the serving that produced it.

EXTEND THE -051/-071 HARNESS: a case where the deterministic client returns an empty reply having consumed its full budget, asserting the run reaches a workflow terminal that names the provider failure. Simulate the condition end to end (convention 22).
Prove it by breaking it: remove the terminal emission and show the assertion fail.
Do NOT change verdict semantics, gate routing, loop conditions or thresholds.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.

questions: Is a truncated reply already retried by the schema-retry path, or does it bypass it? The answer decides whether this is a visibility fix or a retry-path fix.

Should a provider that truncates on a tier disqualify the serving for that tier, the way a schema-refusing serving is disqualified? That is a serving-selection ruling and the owner's; report what the ledger already records about this serving.
